description: Retrieve the citation network for an opinion cluster. Supports two directions: "cited_by" (opinions that cite this one — measures precedential influence) and "citing" (opinions this one cites — reveals the authority chain relied on). This is the primary tool for tracing legal precedent chains. Note: the free tier supports shallow traversal — following 1–2 hops of a single case is practical; deep multi-hop analysis burns through the daily budget quickly.

cluster_id.description: Opinion cluster ID to retrieve citations for. Obtain from courtlistener_search_opinions or courtlistener_lookup_citation.

court.description: Filter results to a specific court (e.g., "scotus", "ca9"). Applies to both directions.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor field.

direction.description: "cited_by" (default): opinions that cite this one — measures precedential influence and downstream adoption. "citing": opinions this one cites — reveals the authority chain the court relied on.

filed_after.description: Limit to citations filed after this date (ISO 8601). For "cited_by", useful for "how has this precedent been applied recently?"

page_size.description: Number of results to request (default 20). For direction="cited_by", CourtListener enforces a minimum of 20 results per page regardless of the value passed — you will always receive at least 20 results. direction="citing" returns at most page_size (the cited-opinion list is sliced before querying) — fewer when the opinion cites fewer than page_size distinct opinions. Either direction costs three requests against the rate limit (a case with many opinion variants costs one more per extra variant page) — keep low for multi-hop traversal.

name: courtlistener_get_citations

direction.description: Direction of the citation relationship returned.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `not_found`: Cluster ID does not exist in CourtListener. Both directions resolve the source cluster before searching, so a bad ID fails here rather than returning an empty network. `rate_limited`: 429 from CourtListener, or no request slot opened within the wait budget. `invalid_date`: filed_after is not a valid ISO 8601 calendar date. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

next_cursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page; null when no more results.

notice.description: Context when no citations are returned — either that this page had no match under the filters and more pages remain, or a recovery hint echoing direction and filters.

results.description: Related opinions in the citation network.

items.description: Related opinion in the citation network.

case_name.description: Case name of the related opinion.

citations.description: Citation strings for the related opinion.

cite_count.description: This opinion's own citation count — its authority weight.

cluster_id.description: Cluster ID of the related opinion.

court.description: Court that issued the related opinion.

court_id.description: Court identifier for use in filter parameters.

date_filed.description: Date the related opinion was filed.

snippet.description: Matched text excerpt from the related opinion, taken from the first opinion variant in the cluster that carries one; empty string when none does. It is a relevance preview for the cluster, not necessarily text surrounding the citation itself.

source_case_name.description: Case name for the source cluster.

source_cluster_id.description: The cluster ID this citation network is for.

totalCount.description: Total citations in the requested direction. For "cited_by" it counts matching clusters with the court and filed_after filters applied. For "citing" it counts the distinct opinions this case cites, before any filter — so it exceeds what the filters make reachable, and runs higher than the result rows, which are clusters (several cited opinions in one case collapse to one row).

title: Get Citation Network
